findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

CFPM for the facility has an expired license (2023). See that at least one member is a certified food protection manager for the facility. At least one CFPM is needed for the events (such as a the Lenten fish fry occurring today). Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

(REPEAT) Observed no operating sani bucket upon start of inspection. Discussed with CFPM and volunteers. Sani bucket was created with quaternary ammonium tablets. Test strips available. Ensure a sani bucket is made before start of food preparation. 400 ppm. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(Repeat situation) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, no sanitizers were available for use at the bar or in the food prep area. PIC provided Quat based sanitizer and made up both the three part sink in the bar area and a spray bottle for the food prep area upon inspector request.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: No CFM information is available in our system or readily available by the establishment during the time of inspection. Ensure a CFM is present during all hours of operation and that their certification information is available upon request.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Upon start of inspection, there was no sanitizer bucket available. Upon inspector request, a sanitizer sink was created. Upon testing, bubbles had formed in the sanitizer sink and the bleach concentration was recorded at 10ppm. Ensure dish detergent is not added to the sanitizer solution to prevent degradation of the chlorine concentration. The solution was drained and then a new solution was created and measured at 200ppm bleach.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The knife holder in the storage closet was observed to be bare wood with an excess of dust buildup. Ensure the knife holder is either removed and painted/sealed in a manner that makes it smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable, or replace the knife holder with a food grade material.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-501.14: The fryer hoods were observed to be coated in grease and other debris. Hood cleaning service sticker from C.F.B. states that the hoods have not been cleaned since 9-22-15. Ensure a hood cleaning service is contracted and cleans the hoods to prevent potential contamination of the food.
6-501.14: (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surfaces should be wash, rinsed and sanitized often enough to maintain them clean to sight and touch. The tray of the ice machine is observed with multiple black spots (assumed to be mold) in it. The tray was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.
No CFM present at time of inspection. This is an ongoing issue at this facility.

findings.comment:
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

Observed the blade of the can opener to be soiled with dried on debris. Discussed with the person in charge and instructed to clean at each closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

Observed the inside of the microwave to be soiled with accumulated food splash. Discussed with the person in charge and instructed to clean often enough so as to prevent accumulation.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

No FSSMC was available and no certification was observable by the inspector during the inspection.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Observed mold growing on the condenser tray in the ice machine. Instructed the PIC to clean regularly to ensure ice doesn't become contaminated.

findings.comment: 750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food. findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed the light shields missing in the back storage area where food is stored. Shield the bulbs.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed the wood shelving in the walk-in cooler to no be properly sealed. Seal the wood shelving. Also, there is a wood beam holding the 3-compartment sink of the bar steady. this wood beam is not sealed. Finally, the lid of the reach-in cooler in the back of the kitchen has a damaged lid (insulation interior is visible). Make sure that wood surfaces are properly sealed so they are smooth and able to be cleaned with a wet wiping cloth. The lid of the reach-in freezer needs a good cleaning along the gasket and then use silicon caulking/glue to insure that interior surfaces are not able to contact moisture of air. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Also, the air return along the wall by the kitchen three compartment is covered with dust. Clean the air return and shelving. Finally, is appears a small cabinet to the react left of the chicken coop area has some prior mold damage. Paint (with Kilz or other mold deterrent ) as needed to remove spores. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1050 An old waste water pan filled with mold was observed beneath the bar three compartment sink. The pan was removed from the kitchen during the inspection. See violation #36. It appears that one of the ice wells was emptied and either leaked or was not completely dumped all the way. Water overflowed onto the floor and left a growth of mold along the back wall of the three compartment sink. All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment: 750.100: Observed chili being reheated from frozen. The chili had been prepared at facility, frozen, and was being reheated on the stove to boiling, and was at 137 degrees F during inspection, and will be held hot in the steam table. Discontinue the practice of cooling and reheating immediately. Any food that is hot shall be used, discarded, or taken home the same day.  Do not cool any food. The Grand Knight voiced understanding. We discussed upgrading to a High Risk if facility would like to cool and reheat.  **During inspection, the chili was brought back up to 170 F.
